text:
The ring has seven stages: vout drives n0, n0 drives n1, and so on through n5 back to vout. Mn1 is the only NMOS whose gate is not its stage's input node. Its gate is `sn2`, which is the tail node of the stage-2 pulldown (Mn2/Mc2), where it should be `n0`, the output of stage 0. That breaks the signal path around the ring, so stage 1 cannot switch. The result is no oscillation, which matches the swing of about 1e-15 V and the failed frequency and tuning-ratio specs.

```json
{"ranking": ["Mn1", "Mn2", "Mc1"], "fault": "Wrong gate connection on Mn1: gate tied to sn2 (stage-2 NMOS tail node) instead of n0 (stage-0 output, the input to stage 1). This breaks the inverter ring chain, so the ring cannot oscillate (swing ~0), and f_mid and tuning ratio fail."}
```
